questions.prompt: In the field of false memory research, this widely-used experimental procedure—named after the researchers who developed and refined it—involves presenting a list of related words to induce recall of a non-presented related word. What is this paradigm called (three-word acronym)?
questions.explanation: The DRM (Deese-Roediger-McDermott) paradigm is a procedure used in memory research to reliably induce false memories, where participants study lists of semantically related words and often falsely recall a related 'lure' word that was never presented.

questions.prompt: In the assassination of President James A. Garfield, he was shot on July 2, 1881, but did not die until later that year due to complications and infection. How many days did Garfield survive after being shot before he died?
questions.explanation: Garfield was shot on July 2, 1881, and died on September 19, 1881, meaning he survived for 79 days after being shot, largely due to infection from his wound and the medical treatment he received.

questions.prompt: In the 1990 Jamaat al Muslimeen coup attempt in Trinidad and Tobago, for how many days did the standoff/crisis last before the insurgents surrendered?
questions.explanation: The coup attempt began on July 27, 1990, and the insurgents surrendered on August 1, 1990, making the crisis last 6 days.

questions.prompt: The Observable Universe article notes that due to the expansion of space, the universe's observable diameter is much larger than what light-speed travel time alone would suggest. What is the estimated diameter of the observable universe?
questions.explanation: The observable universe has an estimated diameter of about 93 billion light-years, even though the universe is only about 13.8 billion years old. This is because space itself has been expanding since the Big Bang, allowing light from distant objects to reach us from much farther away than 13.8 billion light-years.

questions.prompt: In the Moon's Wikipedia article, it explains why we only ever see one side of the Moon from Earth. What is this phenomenon called?
questions.explanation: The Moon is tidally locked with Earth, meaning its rotation period matches its orbital period—a phenomenon called synchronous rotation—which causes the same side to always face Earth.
